title: Recycling rates in Ashford
prompt: The graph below gives information about the percentage of four household materials that were recycled in the town of Ashford between 2000 and 2024. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: Percentage of household materials recycled, Ashford, 2000 to 2024

sentences.text: The line graph compares the proportion of four types of household waste that were recycled in Ashford in 2000, 2008, 2016 and 2024.
sentences.why: Paraphrases the prompt without copying: "compares" replaces "gives information about", "proportion" replaces "percentage" and "types of household waste" replaces "materials". It states what, where and when with no data or opinion.

sentences.text: Overall, recycling rates rose for glass, plastic and metal, whereas paper was the only material to decline by the end of the period.
sentences.why: Identifies the general trend and the one exception in a single sentence. "Whereas" separates the pattern from the exception, and the absence of numbers meets the key Task Achievement requirement for an overview.

sentences.text: Plastic grew fastest, climbing from the lowest rate to well above metal, while glass finished as the most recycled material.
sentences.why: The second overview point selects the biggest change and the final ranking. "Fastest", "well above" and "the most recycled" compare the lines without figures, showing selection and comparison.

sentences.text: Glass and paper were the two most recycled materials throughout the period.
sentences.why: Topic sentence that groups the two leading lines. "Throughout the period" is a general statement that frames the paragraph and supports Coherence before any figures are introduced.

sentences.text: Paper recycling climbed from 55 per cent in 2000 to a peak of 66 per cent in 2016 before falling to 58 per cent in 2024.
sentences.why: Gives the start, the peak and the final value in one sentence. "Climbed from ... to ... before falling to" is an accurate trend structure, and the correct unit supports accuracy and lexical range.

sentences.text: Glass, in contrast, rose steadily from 40 per cent to 64 per cent, which allowed it to overtake paper in the final year.
sentences.why: "In contrast" sets up the comparison and the relative clause "which allowed it to overtake paper" links the two lines. It shows a rank change with exact figures and good grammatical range.

sentences.text: The gap between the two materials had narrowed to just six percentage points by 2016, before the lines crossed.
sentences.why: A short supporting detail that explains the crossing. "Percentage points" is the correct unit for a difference between percentages, and the past perfect shows the narrowing happened first.

sentences.text: Plastic and metal started from much lower levels, but both were recycled far more by 2024.
sentences.why: Topic sentence for the second group. "Started from much lower levels" and "far more by 2024" preview both the starting position and the direction of change, supporting Coherence and Cohesion.

sentences.text: Plastic recycling was negligible at 8 per cent in 2000, yet it increased sharply to 50 per cent by 2024, the biggest rise of any material.
sentences.why: Pairs the start and end values with "yet" for contrast. The apposition "the biggest rise of any material" ranks the data and links back to the overview, earning accuracy and cohesion.

sentences.text: Metal rose more gradually, from 30 per cent to 46 per cent, so plastic overtook it between 2016 and 2024.
sentences.why: Contrasts the pace of two changes with "more gradually" and reports a rank change. The conjunction "so" shows the consequence, giving a flowing comparison rather than two separate statements.

sentences.text: By 2024, only 18 percentage points separated the most recycled material from the least recycled.
sentences.why: Closes the report with a final comparison of the highest and lowest values. The calculated difference shows control of the data, and the sentence adds a new point without a conclusion.

analysis: The instruction is "Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant". With four lines and four dates, you must group and compare the materials, not narrate every point.
What must be covered: the direction of each material from 2000 to 2024, the one material that fell (paper), the fastest growth (plastic) and the change in rank at the top between paper and glass.

Paraphrase: "graph" becomes line graph; "percentage recycled" becomes proportion or rate of recycling; "household materials" becomes types of household waste; "between 2000 and 2024" becomes over the 24-year period.
Key features: plastic rises from 8 to 50, the biggest rise; glass overtakes paper in 2024 (64 against 58); paper peaks at 66 in 2016 and then falls; metal rises steadily from 30 to 46.
Group by similar behaviour: Body 1 for the two leaders (paper and glass), Body 2 for the two lower lines (plastic and metal) that grew from a lower base.
Do not explain why recycling changed (for example new laws or campaigns) because the graph does not say so, and do not predict rates after 2024.

plan.idea: Paraphrase: the line graph compares the proportion of four types of household waste recycled in Ashford in 2000, 2008, 2016 and 2024. No data.
Glass, plastic and metal rose while paper fell at the end. Plastic grew fastest and glass finished as the most recycled. No figures.
Paper 55 to a peak of 66 in 2016, then 58. Glass 40 to 64 and overtook paper in 2024. The gap was six points in 2016.
Plastic 8 to 50, the biggest rise. Metal 30 to 46, overtaken by plastic. Only 18 points between highest and lowest in 2024.
